The subject examines analogue and digital communication protocols and services at the application, network, data link and physical layers including IP and MAC addressing. The subject content includes: • fundamental principles of communication systems • basic structures of computer network systems including local area networks (LAN) and wide area networks (WAN) • essential components of communication systems • simple components of computer network devices • characteristics of signals encountered in communication systems • comparing analogue and digital communications • report writing relevant to this subject including the use of network testing software • TCP/IP and OSI layers

BIT372 - Capstone Experience 2 
Outline period: Semester 1, 2026
Subject description: This is the second of two 12 credit point Capstone Experience subjects delivered in third year of the course. It is designed to consolidate theory and practice gained in the course through the scoping, planning and development of a project. Students are encouraged to work together in teams across different IT majors to develop a solution to a real-world industry or simulated problem. The project from the first capstone subject will be completed in this unit. Where possible, students are encouraged to develop a project involving innovation and entrepreneurship. Topic: • Sprint Plan • Agile Project Development, Scrum Methodology • Collaborative Research and Innovation • Product Breakdown Structure, Design Artefacts, Prototypes • Project Management e.g., Communication Methods, Leadership and Project Supervision • Industry Insights Sharing • Post Project Review Report • Project Poster, Reflective Artefacts • Project Deliverable (Technical document, User Manual, System Demonstration) Student Subject Outline< Capstone Experience 2> <SEM 1 2026>
Learning outcomes: Collaboratively develop and manage a complex IT project from conception to completion, according to industry standards.; Justify and apply IT solutions to complex business problems within a problem-solving framework.; Critically review technical and generic skills against industry professional standards to refine professional practice.; Align IT solutions with ethical, cybersecurity and societal contexts of business environments.; Present project outcomes and communicate solutions to a diverse audience, responding to feedback for improvement.
Assessment overview (outline snapshot): All assessments (except for final examination) and feedback are provided via the Moodle site and in classes.
